newsitem.title: USA: US homebuilders sue Army Corps on wetlands permits.
newsitem.headline: US homebuilders sue Army Corps on wetlands permits.

text.p: The National Association of Home Builders said Friday it sued U.S. Army Corps of Engineers to try to block stricter new wetlands protections that the homebuilders said would slow construction and add to housing costs.

In its lawsuit filed in U.S. District Court in Washington, D.C., the home builders claimed the Army Corps failed to get public comment on some of the changes it made in its permits program for isolated wetlands of up to 10 acres.

The Corps in December released a plan to phase out the Nation 26 permit program, under which landowners could get permits to develop up to 10 acres of wetlands with minimal government review or interference.
Environmentalists said the program was a major loophole in wetlands protections and resulted in destruction of thousands of acres that were important for wildlife, flood control and water quality.
But home builders and other developers opposed the phasing in of stricter wetlands controls which they said would cause unnecessary delays as additional permits were processed.

In their lawsuit, the home builders said the Corps added provisions in its rules that were announced as final in December without first having a public comment period. The new rules took effect on February 11.

The lawsuit also said the two-year time frame the Corps imposed on itself to develop a new permit system with more individual review for small wetlands was "arbitrary and capricious," and said the Corps could provide no assurance the new system would be in place by then.
Comment from the Army Corps was not immediately available.
